entities.name: Adalbero III of Luxembourg
entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Adalbero III of Luxembourg (c. 1045–1072) was Bishop of Metz from 1047 to 1072, one of the most turbulent periods in the Diocese of Metz's history. He was a member of the House of Luxembourg — the dynasty that would eventually produce four Holy Roman Emperors — and his episcopate occurred during the investiture controversy's early phase, when the relationship between the papacy and the German episcopate was being violently contested.

The House of Luxembourg's control of the Metz see was part of the broader pattern of aristocratic dynasties accumulating bishoprics to secure family interests. Adalbero III's episcopate was caught up in the conflicts between imperial and reform interests that preceded the formal outbreak of the Investiture Controversy. His tenure coincided with the beginning of Pope Gregory VII's reform papacy, which would challenge the entire system of lay investiture on which the Ottonian Reichskirche depended.

His membership in the Luxembourg dynasty gave him connections across the Empire. The Luxembourgs' eventual imperial ambitions were grounded in exactly the kind of combined ecclesiastical-secular power base that Adalbero III represented. His episcopate contributed to the family's accumulation of prestige and influence in the Lotharingian corridor that would eventually make them one of Europe's most powerful dynasties.
